test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an example of combination reaction?

options.text: Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime
Formation of water from H₂(g) and O₂(g)
Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight

solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A combination reaction involves two or more substances combining to form a single new substance.
 
• Burning of natural gas is a combustion reaction, which is a type of combination reaction.
 
• Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime, which is a combination reaction.
 
• Formation of water from H₂(g) and O₂(g) is a combination reaction.
 
• Silver chloride turning grey in sunlight is a decomposition reaction, not a combination reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reactions**

 
 
• These reactions involve a single compound breaking down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Example: 2HgO(s) → 2Hg(l) + O₂(g).
 
 
 
• **Combustion Reactions**
 
 
• These are reactions where a substance combines with oxygen to produce heat and light.
 
• Example: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• These reactions involve an element displacing another element in a compound.
 
• Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.
